quote: In your experience, how you guys compare price wise to what they're doing is, I guess, the greater question.
stewart_read: This is a closer-tier pricing/comparison question the rep should have bridged to the specialist immediately.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been strategically stalling to build rapport before redirecting, but no redirect ever comes.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch line ('that's exactly what our specialist is built to answer') the moment pricing/comparison questions surface.

quote: I'll be honest. I'm not too sure. I just I just dealt with the scheduling side of things.
stewart_read: Rep admits the gap transparently (better than fabricating) but fails to recover with a redirect to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Admitting scheduling-only role could be read as honest micro-trade, but it invites more technical grilling instead of closing it off.
coaching_implication: After admitting a gap, immediately pivot: 'that's exactly why I get our design specialist involved — let's get you on their calendar.'

quote: Yeah. Let me pull something out real quick.
stewart_read: Rep tries to look up panel specs live rather than declining the rabbit hole, prolonging a debate he can't win.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a good-faith attempt to build credibility by trying to answer, but it keeps the call in closer territory for minutes longer.
coaching_implication: Don't chase the customer's math — redirect to the design team who will produce the real layout.

quote: one of the things you said upfront immediately gives me pause.
stewart_read: Customer directly states the rep created doubt; rep responds with clarification only, no reframe back to bill/utility pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged a technical clarification was needed first before any flip — reasonable in the moment, but no flip ever follows later either.
coaching_implication: When customer voices doubt, pivot back to what's costing them now (their Dominion bill) rather than re-explaining mechanics.

quote: Yeah. So it'll take me two months to get that to you.
stewart_read: Customer hands rep a timing constraint (not moved in, no usage yet); rep pivots to square footage but never re-anchors on the eventual bill or creates urgency about it.
alternative_hypothesis: Using square footage is the correct schema-sanctioned workaround, so this is procedurally fine, but the bill itself is never flagged for follow-up.
coaching_implication: Note a specific bill follow-up date/method in the handoff so it isn't dropped entirely.

stewart_read: Appointment time is set but rep skips the one-hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair?' handshake.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be intentionally brief because it's a phone-only, low-friction booking, but the schema treats these elements as required regardless.
coaching_implication: Always close with the full button-up sequence to reduce no-show risk, even on short calls.
